public_comments.speaker: SPEAKER_07
public_comments.reason: The speaker is addressing the council regarding a proclamation for Hispanic Heritage Month.
public_comments.text: Proclamation for the governor. Por lo cuanto, en vez de la herencia hispana, es una oportunidad para celebrar las ricas tradiciones culturales y honrar las contribuciones y los logros significativamente de nuestra comunidad hispana y latinoamericana en medicina, leyes, negocio, tecnología, compromiso civil, gobierno y cultura. Y por lo cuanto, los latinoamericanos son el grupo minatorio ético más grande en los Estados Unidos, con 68 millones y la comunidad minoritaria más creciente rápidamente en Pennsylvania con 1.2 millones y por lo cuanto los latinos americanos han servido con distinción en los conflictos militares desde la regla de la revolución y continúa a defender nuestro país hoy en día como miembros de las Fuerzas Armadas. Estos hombres y mujeres valientes nos dan honor y estamos agradecidos por su servicio y sacrificio. Y por lo cuanto, la dedicación de los hispanos y latinoamericanos en las comunidades es una parte integral de Pennsylvania. Han hecho contribuciones en nuestra sociedad diversa a compartir su cultura y talento. Y por lo cuanto, no importa cómo se vea, de dónde venga, a quién ame y ni a quién rece, usted tiene un lugar en Pennsylvania y este estado engullece en un rey las historias y las contribuciones de los hispanos y latinoamericanos en nuestro estado y en toda la nación. Por lo tanto, yo, Josh Shapiro, gobernador de Pennsylvania, proclamo por el presente el 15 de septiembre hasta el 15 de octubre de 2025 como el mes de la herencia hispanidad. El reconocimiento a los hispanos y latinoamericanos pasado y presente en nuestro estado. Animo a todos los residentes de Pennsylvania a celebrar esta importante observancia.

public_comments.text: Good evening. You know me, I'm Frank or Coleo from old Trinity place. And I'm the one who is appealing the the data center ruling by the zoning officer in back in February calling data center a warehouse you you on the council have requested a process to go through not to cut myself short but but it but in any case you have requested the beginning of a process that i believe is its next step is that you're going to look at a draft ordinance on october 6th that's what i understand but but what i have here for you is something that could shortcut the process which is kind of our idea of what a draft ordinance would be to regulate data centers first thing let me talk about what a data center is a data center is a facility whose Its primary purpose is the centralized storage, processing, management, or dissemination of digital data, information, or applications. This includes, but is not limited to, server forms, cloud computing hubs, co-location centers, and telecommunication switching hubs. Data centers typically house large-scale computer systems and supporting infrastructure such as backup generators, cooling systems, and uninterruptible power supplies. That does not sound like a warehouse to me, I have to say. The uses that we would suggest are conditional uses for both the C3, CM, and SM, all three of those zones. What would be some of the restrictions? Well, going to page three, energy use. Data centers shall operate on 100% renewable energy for all electrical and cooling needs, either through on-site generation or verifiable power purchase agreements. Backup generators should meet or exceed EPA Tier 4 final admission standards, and the facility should not require upgrades to the grid, the municipal electric distribution infrastructure, unless all those upgrades are fully paid for by the applicant. Water and cooling systems, I'll only go over the first provision, all water used for cooling operations or operations shall be non-potable, and all discharges shall be treated to a level equal or better than the affluent standard of the city. Going on to, I'm doing this a little bit out of order, noise emissions should not exceed 50 decibels at any property line, and a period of public informational meeting shall be held. The city may require a community benefits agreement as part of it. And then finally, a decommissioning plan shall outline procedures for the safe removal of server infrastructure, hazardous materials, batteries, electronic waste, all that kind of stuff, backed up by a substantial performance bond in case they decide that the data center glut has gotten a hold and they just wanna throw the keys up on the roof and leave us to clean it up. Those are suggested ordinance capable of Mr. Dastra and others that we would like to be considered as part of the ultimate zoning ordinance amendment for data centers. Thank you.
